name: cresva-mcp-server

tools.name: list_brands
tools.description: List the brands on this Cresva account, each with the ad platforms it has connected, its status, and when it last synced. Call this FIRST whenever you do not already know which brand id to use, because every other ad performance tool needs one. Takes no arguments and is one of the cheapest calls here. Returns what Cresva has on the account, so a brand that was never set up will not appear. Needs a Cresva API key.

tools.name: list_campaigns
tools.description: List a brand's campaigns that actually delivered in a window, each with its campaign id, the platform it ran on, what it spent and when it last delivered. Call this whenever you need a campaign id and do not have one, which is every time before compare_campaigns, and to find out what a brand is currently running. Ordered by spend, so the campaigns that matter come first. Returns only campaigns with delivery in the range, so a campaign that has been off all month will not appear: widen date_range to see it. Spend is labelled with the currency the ad account reports in, and there is deliberately no account total, because summing across accounts reporting in different currencies produces a number nobody can act on. Needs a Cresva API key.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Use list_brands if you do not have it.

date_range.description: How far back to look for delivery. Campaigns with no delivery in the window are not listed.

platform.description: Which ad platform to read. Defaults to all of them combined.

limit.description: How many campaigns to return, highest spend first.

tools.name: get_campaign_metrics
tools.description: Read what a brand's ads actually did: spend, revenue, ROAS, CPA, CPC, CPM, CTR, CVR, impressions, clicks, conversions and purchases. Works at account, campaign, ad set or ad level, over a named date range, with optional breakdowns by age, gender, country, platform, placement or device. Call this when someone asks how a brand, a campaign or an ad performed over a period. Returns rows plus totals. The numbers come from the ad data Cresva has already synced from Meta, Google and TikTok, so they reflect the last completed sync rather than what the platform's own dashboard is showing this minute. A brand whose ad accounts are not connected gets an explicit empty answer rather than a screen of zeroes. Needs a Cresva API key.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Use list_brands if you do not have it.

date_range.description: The period to report on. Use 'custom' with start_date and end_date for anything else.

start_date.description: Start date as YYYY-MM-DD. Required when date_range is 'custom'.

end_date.description: End date as YYYY-MM-DD. Required when date_range is 'custom'.

level.description: How far down to break the numbers. Account level is the whole brand.

breakdowns.description: Optional splits, for example by country or device.

platform.description: Which ad platform to read. Defaults to all of them combined.

sort_by.description: Metric to sort by, for example 'spend'.

tools.name: compare_campaigns
tools.description: Put two to ten campaigns, ad sets or ads side by side on the metrics you name, over one shared date range so the numbers are actually comparable. Call this when someone is choosing between them: picking an A/B winner, deciding what to scale, deciding what to switch off. Returns one row per entity. Reads the same synced ad data as get_campaign_metrics, so the same freshness caveat applies. Needs a Cresva API key.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Use list_brands if you do not have it.

entity_ids.description: The campaign, ad set or ad ids to compare. Between two and ten.

level.description: What kind of entity the ids are.

date_range.description: One shared period, so the numbers are comparable.

platform.description: Which ad platform the ids belong to.

tools.name: detect_anomalies
tools.description: Find what changed unexpectedly in a brand's ad performance: CPA spikes, ROAS drops, spend surges, conversion dips. Call this when someone asks what went wrong, or before a client check-in when you want to walk in already knowing. Returns each anomaly with a severity, the campaign or ad set it affects, and the likeliest cause, scored against the brand's own recent history rather than an industry rule of thumb. Computed from the synced ad data, so a brand with only a few days of history will surface little. Needs a Cresva API key.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Use list_brands if you do not have it.

date_range.description: How far back to look for unexpected changes.

platform.description: Which ad platform to read. Defaults to all of them combined.

tools.name: get_pacing_status
tools.description: Answer whether a brand is on track to spend its monthly budget, and what it will land on if nothing changes. Call this for a mid-month check, or when someone asks whether they are going to overspend. Returns spend so far against expected spend to date, a projected end-of-month figure, and a flag where an account or campaign is pacing over or under against its cap or KPI target. The targets are the ones configured in Cresva, so a brand with no budget set will get pacing without a target to judge it against. Needs a Cresva API key.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Use list_brands if you do not have it.

platform.description: Which ad platform to read. Defaults to all of them combined.

level.description: Pace the whole brand, or each campaign separately.

include_projections.description: Include where the month is projected to land.

tools.name: forecast_performance
tools.description: Read the forecast Cresva has already computed for a metric: spend, revenue, ROAS, CPA, conversions, CPC or CTR. Call this when someone asks where a number is heading. IT RETURNS A STORED FORECAST, OR SAYS PLAINLY THAT NONE EXISTS. It does not generate one on demand, so a brand that has not been through Cresva's forecasting job gets an explicit 'no forecast available' rather than a number. Do not describe the result as a live prediction or as something computed for this question; it is a lookup of work done earlier. When a forecast does exist it comes with a confidence interval, and the interval is the part worth quoting. Needs a Cresva API key.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Use list_brands if you do not have it.

metric.description: Which metric to look the forecast up for.

horizon_days.description: How far ahead the forecast should reach.

entity_id.description: A specific campaign or ad set id, if not the whole account.

platform.description: Which ad platform to read. Defaults to all of them combined.

include_ci.description: Include the confidence interval, which is the part worth quoting.

include_drivers.description: Include the drivers behind the forecast, such as seasonality or a budget change.

tools.name: get_benchmarks
tools.description: Compare a brand's CTR, CVR, CPC, CPM, ROAS or CPA against an industry benchmark. Call this when someone asks whether a number is good, rather than just what it is. WHERE THE BENCHMARK COMES FROM MATTERS AND THE RESPONSE TELLS YOU: every answer carries a benchmark_source field naming the provenance of the row it used, and that provenance is not the same for every industry and day. Read that field and say where the comparison came from; when it is null there is no benchmark row for that industry and day and you should say so rather than implying the brand is average. Treat the result as a directional comparison, not an audited market figure. Needs a Cresva API key.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Use list_brands if you do not have it.

platform.description: Which ad platform to benchmark on.

tools.name: get_budget_recommendation
tools.description: Suggest where a brand's budget should move, under constraints you give it: a CAC cap, a ROAS floor, a minimum daily spend per campaign. THIS IS THE SLOWEST TOOL IN THIS SERVER. It reads performance history and forecasts and runs an allocation pass, so it takes noticeably longer than every other call here. Do not call it speculatively or to fill out an answer; call it when someone has actually asked what to change. Returns proposed shifts per campaign with the expected impact of each. IT RECOMMENDS ONLY. Nothing is applied to any ad account by this tool or by this server, and no budget changes as a result of calling it. Needs a Cresva API key.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Use list_brands if you do not have it.

total_budget.description: Total monthly budget to allocate, in the account's currency.

min_roas.description: Lowest acceptable return on ad spend.

min_spend_per_campaign.description: Floor on daily spend per campaign.

constraints.description: Business constraints the recommendation must respect.

platform.description: Which ad platform to read. Defaults to all of them combined.

optimization_goal.description: What the allocation should optimise for.

tools.name: ask_cresva
tools.description: Ask a marketing performance question about a brand in plain language. THIS IS THE FALLBACK. Use a specific tool whenever one fits: get_campaign_metrics for performance, detect_anomalies for what changed, get_pacing_status for budget pacing, compare_campaigns for a head to head. Reach for this one only when the question does not fit any of them, or spans several. Returns the rows it found alongside the interpretation it made of the question, so you can tell the user how it was read and be corrected. Quote that interpretation back; a confident table with an invisible reading behind it is how a wrong answer survives. Reads the same synced ad data as the other tools here. Needs a Cresva API key.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Use list_brands if you do not have it.

question.description: The question, in plain language, as the user asked it.

platform.description: Which ad platform to read. Defaults to all of them combined.

tools.name: get_profit
tools.description: Read whether a brand actually made money, not just revenue: contribution margin, gross profit, ad spend against what the shop banked, break-even ROAS and CPA, the fee-loaded target ROAS, and which SKUs lose money at their current price. Call this whenever someone asks about profit, margin, break-even, or whether a ROAS figure is good, because a ROAS is only good or bad against a break-even and this is the tool that knows the break-even. Profit here is measured against STORE revenue, which is what the shop banked, never the ad platform's attributed revenue. Say so when you quote it. When contribution margin cannot be resolved this returns available: false with the reason, and NO numbers at all. That is deliberate: do not fill the gap with an assumed margin, tell the user which input is missing. The reply names how the margin was determined, and that is worth repeating to the user, because a margin from real product costs and one from a configured percentage deserve different confidence. Needs a Cresva API key.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Use list_brands if you do not have it.

window_days.description: How many days back to measure. Defaults to the last 30.

tools.name: get_memory
tools.description: Read what Cresva has learned about a brand over time: recurring patterns it has spotted, decisions that were taken and how they turned out, and recent questions the team asked. Call this before recommending anything, so you can say whether a brand has tried this before and what happened. Repeating an idea that failed here in March is the fastest way to lose a marketer's trust. This is learned context, not a live metric read. For numbers use get_campaign_metrics. Amounts in these strings are already formatted in the brand's own currency, so quote them as they are rather than converting or re-prefixing them. Needs a Cresva API key.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Use list_brands if you do not have it.

limit.description: How many items of each kind to return.

include.description: Which kinds of learned context to return.

tools.name: list_approvals
tools.description: List the actions a Cresva agent has proposed and is waiting on a human to approve, each with the agent that raised it, what it would touch, the spend cap it may not cross, and when the proposal lapses. Recently decided actions come back too, with their outcome. Call this when someone asks what is waiting on them, what the agents want to do, or why a recommendation has not happened yet. READ ONLY. You cannot approve, reject or expedite anything from here, and there is no tool that can: a person decides in the Cresva app. Say that plainly rather than offering to do it. A null spend cap means none was recorded on that proposal, not that the action is uncapped. Do not describe it as unlimited. Needs a Cresva API key.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Use list_brands if you do not have it.

limit.description: How many proposals to return, pending and recent each.

include_recent.description: Include recently decided actions as well as what is waiting.

tools.name: discover_storefront
tools.description: Check what a brand publishes for AI shopping agents: whether there is an agent-readable storefront at all, and what it supports (search, recommend, compare, negotiate, buy), which currencies and languages, and its rate limits. Call this FIRST when working with a storefront, because it tells you which of the other storefront tools will work for that brand. Returns the brand's published capability manifest, which is what the brand declares about itself rather than anything Cresva measured. No API key and no Cresva account needed.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Storefront tools are public, so this can be a brand you do not own.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Search a brand's catalogue using the words a shopper would actually use, with an optional category filter and price cap. Call this when someone describes what they are looking for rather than naming a product. Returns ranked product cards with price, currency and availability. Matching is done by the storefront, not by you, and it is closer to whole-word matching than to a fuzzy search: a query that returns nothing may mean the catalogue words it differently rather than that the product is absent, so try list_products before telling someone a brand does not sell something. No API key needed.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Storefront tools are public, so this can be a brand you do not own.

query.description: What the shopper is looking for, in their own words.

limit.description: How many results to return. Up to 30.

tools.name: list_products
tools.description: Page through a brand's catalogue in order, rather than searching it. Call this when someone wants to browse, when you need to know how big a catalogue is, or when a search came back empty and you want to check whether the catalogue is empty or just worded differently. Returns product cards with price, currency and availability, plus a total count. No API key needed.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Storefront tools are public, so this can be a brand you do not own.

page.description: Which page of the catalogue. Starts at 1.

limit.description: How many per page. Up to 50.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Read one product in full: price, currency, availability, description, attributes such as colour, size and material, images, and any review summary the storefront publishes. Call this after a search or a listing when you need more than a card, and always before quoting a price to someone as fact. Returns the fields a purchase decision actually needs. No API key needed.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Storefront tools are public, so this can be a brand you do not own.

product_id.description: The product id, as returned by search_products or list_products.

tools.name: compare_products
tools.description: Put two to five products from the same brand side by side on the fields an agent reads: price, availability, attributes, and what differentiates them. Call this when someone is choosing between specific products they have already found. All the products must belong to the same brand; this does not compare across brands. No API key needed.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Storefront tools are public, so this can be a brand you do not own.

product_ids.description: Between two and five product ids, all from the same brand.

tools.name: get_trust_score
tools.description: Read the trust signals a storefront publishes about itself: a composite score out of 100, a tier, the components behind it such as fulfilment reliability and pricing transparency, and any certification. Call this when weighing whether to recommend a brand, alongside price and availability rather than instead of them. A brand with no score yet returns 'unrated' with a message saying so, and unrated means not yet measured, never badly rated. Say it that way. No API key needed.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Storefront tools are public, so this can be a brand you do not own.

tools.name: negotiate_price
tools.description: Open a live price negotiation with a brand for one of its products. THIS IS NOT A READ. It creates a real negotiation session against the brand's own pricing rules, and the reply can be an ACCEPTED OFFER WITH AN ORDER REFERENCE and a hold on the price. Other replies are a counter-offer at a different price, a rejection, or an alternative such as a bundle. CONFIRM THE EXACT NUMBER WITH THE USER BEFORE YOU CALL THIS. Do not pick an offer price yourself, do not round one you were given, and do not call it to find out what would happen. Every call is a fresh negotiation and the brand's rules decide the outcome, not you. Call it only when the user has said what they want to offer and has understood that it may be accepted on the spot. The tool reads the product's list price and currency itself, so you supply only the offer. No API key needed, which means anyone can open a negotiation: treat that as a reason for more care, not less.

brand_id.description: The brand's id in Cresva. Storefront tools are public, so this can be a brand you do not own.

offered_price.description: The price the USER said they want to offer, per unit. Do not invent or round this.

message.description: An optional note to send with the offer.

tools.name: scan_store
tools.description: Point this at any public store URL and it reports whether AI shopping agents can find it, understand what it sells, and buy from it. Returns a three-axis verdict with the individual checks behind each one, quoted evidence from the page, what the store's robots.txt declares per crawler, and specific fixes. NO BRAND ID AND NO API KEY. It works on any public store, including one the user does not own, so it answers both 'is my store ready for AI shoppers' and 'how does this competitor compare'. Takes a few seconds and makes no model calls, so it is cheap to run. This is the tool to reach for when someone names a store by its web address rather than by a Cresva brand.

url.description: The full store URL including https://. A product page gives the fullest answer; a homepage works.

page_kind.description: What the URL points at. Saying 'product' skips a discovery fetch and is faster.

fresh.description: Bypass the one hour cache. Use when the store was just changed.
